audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 3 and 4-5 read 'Skill' in both layers while whys[2] says the Flux loop 'punishes his immobility hard' and whys[3] says your rotation out-trades his Q poke. Packet chart gives Ryze both rows.
audit.why: Swain has no dash; a landed Rune Prison root is a full rotation for free, and that is exactly the level the loop comes online at. 53.88% over 219 games.
audit.corrected: Rows 2 and 3 -> Ryze as matched full/content pairs, ratings 5/10 -> 7/10.

audit.why: Level 3 (loop online vs an immobile target), level 6 (Realm Warp as the exit from a Demonic Ascension drain), and Seraph's are the breakpoints, and spikes[0..3] state them.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page's whole focus was Demonic Ascension, but the ability that actually decides the lane — Nevermove — was described only as 'his E pull', with no mention of Riot's key clause: the wave travels out, 'then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits'. Its 12/11.5/11/10.5/10 cooldown and 850 range were never given. Separately, wants.foe[2] claimed Death's Hand shreds MR; it does not — damage ramps per bolt that hits.
audit.why: Knowing the root is on the return pass changes the dodge entirely: you walk through the outbound wave and then leave its line, instead of backing straight down it. And a player itemising against fake MR shred buys the wrong component.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d and report[5].t now state the return-trip root plus the cooldown; wants.foe[2] rewritten to the per-bolt ramp.

audit.whatIsWrong: The resistances-invalidated interaction was absent: Ravenous Flock's Soul Fragments heal Swain and permanently raise his maximum health, so poke that does not kill feeds him.
audit.why: It reframes chip trading — the anti-heal note in report[8].t covers the healing half but not the permanent HP half, which is why stacking resistances is the wrong answer to him.
audit.corrected: Stated in dontsFull[0].d; Vision of Empire's off-screen reach and free Soul Fragment added to dosFull[2].d.

edits.before: His drain mode — disengage and reset the fight when it starts. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Nevermove only roots on the way back — step through the outbound wave, then move off its return line.

edits.before: Track Swain’s Demonic Ascension: His drain mode — disengage and reset the fight when it starts. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Track Nevermove (12s at rank 1, 850 range): it roots on the return trip, not the way out — dodge the second pass and his combo dies.

edits.before: Swain whiffs Demonic Ascension and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Vision of Empire lands from off-screen — it heals him a fragment too.

edits.before: That is Swain’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Ravenous Flock's soul fragments give him permanent max HP — chip damage funds him.

edits.before: Poke you with Q to shred MR stacks and widen the damage gap before your first item
edits.after: Stack Death's Hand bolts — each extra bolt that hits you raises the damage — before your item

notes: Both packet suspectNames hits are FALSE POSITIVES: 'Stack Demonic Ascension' and 'Full Flux' are correct names in context. One thing I could not verify and therefore left alone: whys[4] and spikes[3] both assert Realm Warp 'exits' a Demonic Ascension drain. Realm Warp teleports allies near the portal after a delay, which is plausible as an escape, but whether it beats a sustained drain is a timing claim the kits do not settle. Also note Demonic Ascension is a flat 120s at every rank — the page never gives the number anywhere, which is a gap worth filling on a pass with more length budget.
